overall: Los Angeles is deep in a classic June Gloom pattern this morning, with temperatures locked in a remarkably flat band of 62–63°F since midnight (ET) under mostly cloudy skies and patchy fog, consistent with a strong marine layer suppressing any diurnal warming. Calm winds (0 mph at last reading) and a moderately high dewpoint (~57°F) underscore the marine influence. No meaningful warming trend has developed yet — velocity is +0.0°F/hr — but this is still very early morning local time (~4:49 PDT), and afternoon burn-off is expected to allow gradual warming toward the day's peak.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show good directional agreement but a modest 2.5°F spread: HRRR is warmest at 69.5°F, ECMWF in the middle at 68.2°F, and NBM coolest at 67.0°F. max_temp_prediction: With fog forecast to persist through 11am PDT, a mostly cloudy sky regime, and light onshore flow, the marine layer will suppress the morning warmup and limit afternoon heating. Model consensus centered near 67–69.5°F, the NWS call of 69°F, and the flat overnight temperature profile all support a daily high in the upper 60s. Confidence is moderate — the primary uncertainty is how aggressively the marine layer burns off; a sluggish burn-off (consistent with current calm winds and high dewpoint) risks keeping the high in the 66–68°F range, while a faster afternoon clearing could push it to 69–70°F. Best estimate is 68.5°F.
